description: The presentation: its theme, slides, and settings.

markdownpoint.description: The format version, as a major and a minor number in quotes: "1.0".

id.description: The presentation's id. The .md file has the same id.

save-id.description: The id of the save that wrote the file. MarkdownPoint writes it while the presentation is shared for editing. Other tools leave it unchanged.

theme.description: The key of the presentation's theme. It's the name of the theme's folder in themes. The theme's master sets the slide size and `unit-scale`.

background.description: The background every slide shows, unless the slide sets its own.

transition.description: The transition from every slide to the next, unless the slide sets its own. Without it, slides cross-dissolve over 0.5 seconds.

soundtrack.description: Music that plays under the whole presentation.

file.description: The audio file, as a presentation's file path.

loop.description: With `repeat`, it plays again from the start when it ends. Without a loop, it plays once.

fade-in.description: How long it takes to rise linearly from silence each time it starts.

fade-out.description: How long it takes to fall linearly to silence before the file ends each time. Where the two fades overlap, the lower volume is used.

self-playing.description: With it, the presentation plays by itself, such as at a kiosk.

slide-delay.description: How long each slide stays after its last step before the next slide.

step-delay.description: How long the presentation waits before each step that would wait for a click.

loop.description: With `repeat`, it starts over after the last slide. Without a loop, it stops there.

countdown.description: How long the talk should take, in seconds. Without it, the talk has no set length.

default-text-style.description: The text style and color of a new text box. Without a text style, a new text box has none. Text boxes already on the slides don't change.

color.description: The color: a color role or a hex color.

image-style.description: The style generated image objects use when they don't set one. It's written as text, and `none`, the default, means no style. A background's image uses `background-image-style` instead.

background-image-style.description: The style generated background images use when their background doesn't set one. It's written as text, and `none`, the default, means no style.

swatches.description: The colors the author has saved for this presentation, as hex colors.

date.description: The date the date field shows, as YYYY-MM-DD. It must be a real calendar date, from year 0001 on.

locale.description: The presentation's language and region, as a BCP 47 tag such as fr-CA. It sets how the date field is written, chart cells are read, and words are split to animate. The default is en-US.

additionalProperties.description: One slide's objects, look, and animation. Its text is in the .md file.

layout.description: The theme layout the slide uses, by key.

scheme.description: The slide's color scheme. If it's left out or the theme doesn't have it, the slide uses its layout's scheme.

background.description: The slide's own background. It replaces the presentation's whole background. A key it leaves out has its default, and an empty background is plain.

skipped.description: Whether the slide is skipped when presenting and exporting. It stays in the presentation.

transition.description: The transition from this slide to the next, or none.

The camera's motion blur. Only the 3D layer is blurred. It is blurred only in exported movies and the Agent's rendered frames.

shutter.description: How long the shutter stays open, in frames of the movie. At 0, there is no blur. The default is 0.5. It can be animated.

frame-position.description: Where the frame's moment falls in the shutter's opening. The default is center.

samples.description: How many moments the 3D layer is drawn at while the shutter is open. The drawings are then averaged. Cinema 4D's Sub-Frame Motion Blur Samples work the same way. The default is 32.

anyOf.description: The camera's render effects: a fast estimate of light bouncing between surfaces, and of the World's light blocked where surfaces meet. In Cinema 4D's Render Settings, they are Global Illumination and Ambient Occlusion. The effects show wherever the 3D layer shows. Only surfaces in view bounce light. A shadow catcher bounces none. An override replaces the whole record.

global-illumination.description: Whether lit surfaces bounce their light onto what is near them. The default is false.

ambient-occlusion.description: Whether the World's light darkens where surfaces close in on each other. A shadow catcher then also darkens where an object rests on it. The default is false.

distance.description: How far bounced light and shading reach from a surface. The default is 400.

anyOf.description: The camera's drift. The camera and its point of interest move together from `from` toward the camera's set position, on the slide's own clock. That clock starts when the slide's transition in begins. It runs on through the slide's steps, waits, and transition out. At t seconds on that clock, while t is less than `duration`, the camera and its point of interest are `from` × (1 − t ÷ `duration`)² away from the set position. They slow steadily and reach the set position when t is `duration`. After that, they are at the set position. Stills and the editor show the set position. A slide has no drift when a scroll transition enters or leaves it.

from.description: Where the camera starts, as an {x, y, z} offset from its set position. An axis left out doesn't move.

duration.description: How many seconds after the slide begins to appear the camera comes to rest.

anyOf.description: A constraint that moves the slide's camera with an object. Cinema 4D's Position constraint works the same way. Only the camera can have it. With a spring, the camera follows the way a keyframe's spring moves. It trails a sudden move, catches up, and settles as the object stops. If the spring is still moving 10 seconds after what it follows has stopped, the camera halts where it got to, short of its target. It stays there until a click moves what it follows again. Every key except `id`, `type`, and `target` can be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as follow. It is unique among the camera's constraints. A step animates its strength as `constraints.follow.strength`.

target.description: The id of the model or light the camera follows.

target-node.description: The name of a node in the target's model, such as ball. The camera follows the node as the model's Action moves it. Without it, the camera follows the target's origin.

axes.description: The 3D space's axes the camera follows on, from x, y, and z. Without it, the camera follows on all three.

relative-to-target.description: Whether the camera follows the target at an offset: its own offset from the slide's center at z 0, added to the target's point. With false, it is at the target's point. The default is true.

strength.description: How far the camera moves to the point it follows, from 0, not at all, to 1, fully. The default is 1. It can be animated.

spring.description: The spring the camera follows on. It has the `amount` and `response` of a keyframe's `spring` interpolation. Without it, the camera follows exactly.

amount.description: How far the camera swings past where the target stops, from 0, not at all, to 1.

response.description: The spring's natural period. A shorter response catches up sooner.

overrides.description: Changes, by id, to what the slide inherits from its layout and master. They're kept even if they match what's inherited. An object set to `null` is removed. The camera and the World can't be removed.

file.description: a file path in the presentation's folder

objects.description: The slide's objects, back to front. Its own objects are written out, and one from its layout or master is listed by its id. An inherited object the list doesn't name is behind all of them.

initial.description: The values of animated parameters before the slide's first step, as "object.parameter" keys such as "card.opacity".

slides.description: The slides, by id. The .md file has their order and text.

additionalProperties.description: A reusable animated scene that slides show as instances. A composition can't contain itself, directly or through another.

name.description: The composition's name, on one line that isn't blank and has no control characters.

scheme.description: The color scheme it's drawn in on its own canvas while it's edited. The default is the light scheme. Each instance uses the scheme of the slide it's on.

items.description: One control a composition offers its instances. Its default matches its type: a number, true or false, a color, one of its options' ids, or a file path for a media control. The objects a media control binds all have the same type. Its default and its values are files of that type.

id.description: The id that names the control in a binding, an instance's value, and a marker. It's unique among the composition's controls.

name.description: The name the author sees, on one line that isn't blank and has no control characters. Two controls can have the same name.

id.description: The id that names the control in a binding, an instance's value, and a marker. It's unique among the composition's controls.

name.description: The name the author sees, on one line that isn't blank and has no control characters. Two controls can have the same name.

default.description: The value used when an instance doesn't set one. A number control's default is from its min to its max. A text control's default text is in the .md file.

min.description: A number control's smallest value, below its max.

max.description: A number control's largest value, above its min.

default.description: The value used when an instance doesn't set one. A number control's default is from its min to its max. A text control's default text is in the .md file.

items.description: One option of a choice control, in the order its pop-up shows them.

id.description: The id that names the option in the control's default, an instance's value, and the value of a key the choice sets. It's unique among the control's options.

name.description: The words the author sees, on one line with no space at either end and no comma: ",", "，" or "、".

options.description: A choice control's options, one or more, in the order its pop-up shows them. Its default is one of their ids.

id.description: The id that names the control in a binding, an instance's value, and a marker. It's unique among the composition's controls.

name.description: The name the author sees, on one line that isn't blank and has no control characters. Two controls can have the same name.

default.description: The value used when an instance doesn't set one. A number control's default is from its min to its max. A text control's default text is in the .md file.

controls.description: The controls each instance can set, in the order they're shown.

objects.description: Its objects, back to front. A composition can't contain a model, a light, a shadow catcher, a floor, a camera, the World, or a text with a `model`.

initial.description: The values of animated parameters before its first step, as "object.parameter" keys.

steps.description: Its steps, played back to back. They have no cues and no `loop-start`. With every pass counted, they last at most 4,294,967,296 seconds.

compositions.description: Reusable animated scenes, by id. Slides show them as instances.

additionalProperties.description: A comment thread pinned to a slide or a composition. Its id is unique among the presentation's threads.

slide.description: The id of the slide it is pinned to. It can name a slide that is no longer there.

composition.description: The id of the composition it is pinned to. It can name a composition that is no longer there.

created.description: When it was written, as a UTC timestamp to the millisecond, such as 2026-10-16T09:30:00.000Z.

text.description: What it says. It isn't blank and has no control characters except line breaks and tabs.

position.description: Where it is pinned, as {x, y} in canvas units on the slide or composition. When the slide size changes, it moves with the slide's objects.

resolved.description: Whether the thread is resolved. The default is false.

additionalProperties.description: One reply in a comment thread. Its id is unique in its thread.

created.description: When it was written, as a UTC timestamp to the millisecond, such as 2026-10-16T09:30:00.000Z.

text.description: What it says. It isn't blank and has no control characters except line breaks and tabs.

replies.description: The replies, by id, each with an author, a created time, and text.

comments.description: Comment threads, by id. Each one is pinned to a slide or a composition.

anchor-point.description: The point an object turns and scales about when it is animated or has an initial value. A group also tilts about it.

x.description: How far across the frame, as a fraction of its width.

y.description: How far down the frame, as a fraction of its height.

area-size.description: An area light's size along its own axes, in canvas units. In Redshift's Area Light, they are Size X and Size Y.

x.description: Its width, along its own x.

y.description: Its height, along its own y.

auto-layout.description: How a group places its members one after another. The defaults are direction vertical, gap 0, align start, and reference-point start. Members are placed in their order in the `objects` list. Hidden members, members with `ignore-auto-layout`, and lines attached to an object are skipped.

direction.description: Whether the members run down or across.

gap.description: The space between one member and the next.

align.description: How the members line up across the layout's direction.

reference-point.description: Which point of the members' box stays at the position as the members grow or shrink: its start, middle, or end along the layout's direction.

position.description: Where the members' box is on the slide, as {x, y}. Depending on `reference-point`, it is the box's top-left corner in the group's rotation, or its middle or end along the layout's direction.

background.description: A slide background: a fill, an image, or an image on a fill.

fill.description: The color or gradient behind everything.

image.description: The image over the fill. It covers the slide and is cropped as with an image's `scale-mode` `fill`.

file.description: The image, as a presentation's file path.

crop.description: How far the image is zoomed, and which point stays in view.

exposure.description: How much lighter or darker the image is. 0 leaves it unchanged.

contrast.description: How much more or less contrast the image has. 0 leaves it unchanged.

saturation.description: How much more or less saturated the image's colors are. 0 leaves them unchanged.

temperature.description: How much warmer or cooler the image's colors are. 0 leaves them unchanged.

grayscale.description: How far the image's colors fade to gray. 0 leaves them unchanged.

drop-shadow.description: A drop shadow behind the image.

prompt.description: The prompt for a generated background image.

image-style.description: The style of a generated background image, as text, or `none` for no style. The default is the presentation's `background-image-style`.

transparent-background.description: Whether a generated background image is made with a transparent background.

restyle.description: A style applied over the image. MarkdownPoint draws it from the image as it was first made.

generation.description: Which image generation record made the background image. For a restyle, it also names the image the restyle was applied to.

color.description: a color role or a hex color

comment-author.description: Who wrote a comment. Its `id` has one of three forms. For a computer's user, it is `local:` followed by a lowercase UUID. For a collaboration service member, it is `shared:` followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits. For a Dropbox user, it is `dropbox:` followed by the Dropbox account id as Dropbox's API spells it. That account id starts with `dbid:`.

id.description: Who wrote it, if known, in one of the record's three forms.

name.description: The name the thread shows for the author. It is one line that isn't blank and has no control characters.

anyOf.description: A constraint that turns a model, or one of its nodes, toward a target. Cinema 4D's Aim constraint works the same way. Every key except `id`, `type`, and `target` can be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as look. It is unique among the model's constraints. A step animates its strength as `constraints.look.strength`.

node.description: The name of the model's node that turns, such as Head. Without it, the whole model turns.

target.description: The id of the model or light whose origin it turns toward. With `camera`, it turns toward the camera.

axis.description: The axis of the model or node that points at the target, in its GLB's axes. In those axes, y is up, and a model faces along +z. The default is y.

strength.description: How far it turns toward the target, from 0, not at all, to 1, fully. It applies to the result of the constraints before it. The default is 1. It can be animated.

anyOf.description: A constraint that keeps a model's volume as the model scales along its own axes. The volume is measured at the model's scale before animation. Every key except `id` and `type` can be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as squash. It is unique among the model's constraints. A step animates its strength as `constraints.squash.strength`.

mode.description: When the volume is kept: with `strict`, under any scale; with `uniform`, while the model scales evenly; with `single-axis`, while only the free axis scales. The default is strict.

free-axis.description: The axis whose scale is animated. The other two follow to keep the volume. The default is y.

volume.description: The volume to keep, as a multiple of the model's volume before animation. The default is 1.

strength.description: How strongly it keeps the volume, from 0, not at all, to 1, fully. The default is 1. It can be animated.

crop.description: An image's or a video's zoom and focus inside its frame.

scale.description: How far it is zoomed. At 1, an image fits its frame as its `scale-mode` sets, and a background covers the slide. Above 1, it is zoomed in. Below 1, it is zoomed out.

focal-point.description: The point that stays in view, as {x, y}. Each is a fraction of the image, across and down.

anyOf.description: A drop shadow. Its keys work like those of Photoshop's Drop Shadow. First, what the object paints grows solid by size × spread. Then it is blurred by a Gaussian whose standard deviation is size × (1 − spread) / √6. The size isn't a blur radius.

size.description: How far it reaches, in canvas units. It is at most 102.878569 when the slide's shorter side is 1080 or less. The limit grows in proportion on a larger slide, to 205.757138 at 3840 × 2160.

spread.description: The fraction of the size that is solid. The rest of the size is blurred. At 1, the shadow is solid all the way out. Photoshop's Spread works the same way.

offset.description: How far it falls, as {x, y} across and down in the object's own axes. It turns and scales with the object and its groups. A flip doesn't mirror it. A background's offset is in the slide's axes.

color.description: Its color: a color role, or a hex color written #RGB or #RRGGBB. A role's alpha is ignored. The shadow's opacity is set by `opacity` alone.

enter.description: Text that enters piece by piece. `based-on` sets whether a piece is a paragraph, a word, or a character. The defaults are interpolation linear, fade-length 1, order forward, spaces off, spread 1, pause 0, and progress 1.

delivery.description: `by-paragraph`: each paragraph enters on the step whose text cue names it. It needs based-on `paragraph` and no seed. Order, spread, pause, and progress must be at their defaults.

duration.description: How long each paragraph takes to enter, in seconds. With interpolation hold, each paragraph appears when its cue is reached. A step that has only paragraphs' cues lasts as long as they take.

from.description: How each piece looks as it starts to enter: opacity, offset, scale, rotation, and blur.

offset.description: How far it starts from where it rests, as {x, y} across and down in ems.

scale.description: Its scale. At 1, it is its own size.

rotation.description: How far it is turned, in degrees clockwise.

blur.description: How blurred it is, by its radius in ems. It is never wider than the widest blur the object key `blur` allows on the slide.

interpolation.description: How each piece moves into place: gradually, or at once with hold. A spring's response and an elastic's period don't apply here.

fade-length.description: How much of each piece's entrance its fade lasts, as a fraction. The fade starts with the move and follows the piece's interpolation.

spaces.description: Whether each space counts as a piece. It applies only with based-on `character`.

order.description: The order the pieces enter in. With a seed, it must be `random`.

seed.description: The seed for a random order: the same seed gives the same order.

spread.description: How many intervals each piece moves for. In forward, backward, or random order, this many pieces move at once.

pause.description: How many intervals the text waits between turns, after the pieces before have arrived.

progress.description: How far the text has entered. It is animated by steps.

exit.description: Text that exits piece by piece. Its pieces are counted and timed the same way as an entrance's pieces. The defaults are interpolation linear, fade-length 1, order forward, spaces off, spread 1, pause 0, and progress 0.

to.description: How each piece looks as it finishes exiting: opacity, offset, scale, rotation, and blur.

offset.description: How far it ends from where it rests, as {x, y} across and down in ems.

scale.description: Its scale. At 1, it is its own size.

rotation.description: How far it is turned, in degrees clockwise.

blur.description: How blurred it is, by its radius in ems. It is never wider than the widest blur the object key `blur` allows on the slide.

interpolation.description: How each piece moves out of place: gradually, or at once with hold. A spring's response and an elastic's period don't apply here.

fade-length.description: How much of each piece's exit its fade lasts, as a fraction. The fade ends with the move and follows the piece's interpolation.

spaces.description: Whether each space counts as a piece. It applies only with based-on `character`.

order.description: The order the pieces exit in. With a seed, it must be `random`.

seed.description: The seed for a random order: the same seed gives the same order.

spread.description: How many intervals each piece moves for. In forward, backward, or random order, this many pieces move at once.

pause.description: How many intervals the text waits between turns, after the pieces before have left.

progress.description: How far the text has exited. It is animated by steps.

flat-scale.description: A flat object's scale along its own axes. The object scales about its frame's center. An animated or initial change of its scale is about its `anchor-point`. Text breaks into lines first, then stretches with the scale.

floor-position.description: A floor's height in the 3D space. A floor is level and goes on without end. Cinema 4D's Floor works the same way. So a floor's position has only y. Without a position, the floor is at the slide's bottom edge.

y.description: How far up from the slide's bottom edge, in canvas units.

frame.description: An object's position and size, in canvas units from the slide's top left. A table's frame has only x and y. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text.

x.description: How far across the left edge is.

y.description: How far down the top edge is.

generation.description: How a generated or restyled image was made.

id.description: The id of the image generation record that made the image. It is the lowercase UUID in the record's file name, `generated/<id>.json`.

original.description: The image a restyle was applied to. It is present only when the record is for a restyle.

file.description: Its file, as a presentation's file path. The path ends in an image's extension.

generation.description: How it was made, if it was generated. Without it, the image wasn't generated.

id.description: The id of its image generation record. It is the lowercase UUID in the record's file name, `generated/<id>.json`.

angle.description: A linear gradient's direction, in degrees clockwise from up.

line.description: Where a linear gradient's line is, in the object's frame. It turns about its middle by `angle`. The default line crosses the box the gradient fills through its center. It is the same in CSS.

x.description: The x of its middle, as a fraction of the frame's width.

y.description: The y of its middle, as a fraction of the frame's height.

length.description: Its length, as a fraction of the frame's diagonal.

stops.description: The gradient's two or more colors, each with its position.

center.description: The center of a radial gradient, as {x, y}.

x.description: Its x, as a fraction of the frame's width. 0 is the left edge, and 1 is the right edge.

y.description: Its y, as a fraction of the frame's height. 0 is the top edge, and 1 is the bottom edge.

shape.description: With `circle`, a radial gradient is round in any box. Without it, the gradient reaches the box's corners.

stops.description: The gradient's two or more colors, each with its position.

image-style-or-none.description: nonempty text without NUL characters, or "none"

line-end.description: A line end attached to an object.

object.description: The id of the object it attaches to.

side.description: Which side of the object it attaches to. With `auto`, it attaches to the nearest side.

last-position.description: Where the end was when it was last drawn, as {x, y}. It is used when the object it attaches to isn't on the slide.

model-node-name.description: the name of one of the model's nodes

nonblank-line.description: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters

file.description: a file path in the presentation's folder

mask.description: SVG path data where 0 to 1 spans the object's frame

geometry.description: SVG path data where 0 to 1 spans the object's frame

text-path.description: SVG path data where 0 to 1 spans the object's frame

file.description: a file path in the presentation's folder

poster.description: a file path in the presentation's folder

opaque-color.description: a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000"

repeater.description: Copies of the object, each moved, turned, scaled, and delayed a little more than the one before. The defaults are 0 for each key, 1 for `scale` and `end-opacity`, and the frame's center for `anchor-point`.

copies.description: How many copies there are. The original counts as one.

position.description: How far each copy moves from the one before, as {x, y} across and down.

rotation.description: How far each copy is turned clockwise from the one before.

scale.description: How much each copy is scaled from the one before. At 1, each copy is the same size as the one before.

anchor-point.description: The point the copies turn and scale about, as {x, y}. Each is a fraction of the frame, across and down.

stagger.description: How much later each copy plays the object's animation than the one before.

end-opacity.description: The last copy's opacity, as a fraction of the object's opacity. The copies between fade toward it.

position-randomness.description: The farthest each copy moves in a random direction.

rotation-randomness.description: The farthest each copy turns either way at random.

scale-randomness.description: The most each copy grows or shrinks at random, as a fraction of its size.

stagger-randomness.description: The most extra time each copy waits at random.

seed.description: The random seed: the same seed gives the same copies.

restyle.description: A style applied over an image or a background's image. It has every key of a library style except `reference-image-prompt`.

name.description: The style's name, on one line that isn't blank and has no control characters.

prompt.description: How the style changes an image, as an edit prompt. It isn't blank.

transparent-background.description: Whether images in the style have transparent backgrounds.

space-euler.description: A 3D object's rotation about its origin, in the 3D space's axes: x right, y up, and z toward the viewer. It is in degrees, or a quaternion in quaternion mode.

x.description: Degrees about x, or a quaternion's x.

y.description: Degrees about y, or a quaternion's y.

z.description: Degrees about z, or a quaternion's z.

space-position.description: A point in the 3D space, in canvas units. The x axis runs right from the slide's left edge, the y axis runs up from its bottom edge, and the z axis runs toward the viewer. The slide is at z 0. The axes are right-handed. glTF and three.js use the same axes. A parented object's position is in its parent's space.

space-quaternion.description: A 3D object's rotation about its origin, in the 3D space's axes: x right, y up, and z toward the viewer. It is in degrees, or a quaternion in quaternion mode.

w.description: A quaternion's w, in quaternion mode only.

x.description: Degrees about x, or a quaternion's x.

y.description: Degrees about y, or a quaternion's y.

z.description: Degrees about z, or a quaternion's z.

space-scale.description: A 3D object's scale along its own axes, about its origin. A negative scale mirrors the object along that axis. Objects parented to a light are scaled with it. An area light's surface is scaled too.

items.description: One step: the moves, cuts, and media starts that a click or the previous step sets off. Its times, and the times of its keyframes and cues, are in seconds, rounded to six decimal places.

id.description: The step's id, unique on its slide.

name.description: The step's name, on one line that isn't blank and has no control characters.

start.description: When the step starts: with the previous step, or after it ends. With either, a first step starts when the slide's transition ends, except under a scroll. Without it, the step waits for a click.

min-duration.description: The least time the step lasts, in seconds. A later keyframe, cue, or entering paragraph makes it longer. Without it, or at 0, the step lasts as long as what is in it.

repeat-count.description: How many times the step plays before it completes. Without it, the step plays once.

loop-start.description: The time it loops back to while waiting for the next click, in seconds into the step. It is before the later of its `min-duration` and its keyframe and cue times, other than a paragraph's entrance.

additionalProperties.description: One parameter's animation in a step: its keyframes and what happens after the last one. A position can also be keyed as one point. `frame.xy` and `translation.xy` have {x, y}, and `position.xyz` has {x, y, z}. Each of their keyframes has every part. A step keys a position either as a point or by its parts, not both. A step that keys both is read with a warning, and the point plays. An initial value sets each part on its own.

items.description: One keyframe: a value a parameter reaches at a time. Two keyframes of one parameter at one time are read with a warning, and the one with the later id plays. A keyframe whose value is `null` clears the whole parameter. The parameter's text style or default then shows. It can't clear a part of a key, a point, `visible`, `rotation`, `scale`, a constraint's strength, `shape-type`, `icon`, or `geometry`.

id.description: The keyframe's id, unique in its step among its keyframes and cues.

start.description: When the move into the keyframe begins, in seconds into the step. It must come before `time`. Without it, the move begins at the previous keyframe.

time.description: When the parameter reaches the value, in seconds into the step.

value.description: The value, written as the parameter is. It can be `null` to clear the whole parameter.

interpolation.description: How the value reaches the keyframe: gradually, or at once with hold. It is a named curve, a named curve with its settings, a cubic Bézier, or a spring. The default is linear.

interrupted.description: The longer move this keyframe interrupts. Up to this keyframe, the motion follows that move's interpolation.

end.description: When it would have ended, in seconds into the step, at or after the keyframe's time.

path.description: A curved motion path for the move into the keyframe. Only a point keyframe can have it.

geometry.description: The path, as SVG path data from the move's start, 0 0, to its end, 1 0. It is one open contour of 2 to 8,192 points. It has at most 1,048,576 characters.

orient.description: Whether the object turns to face along the path.

exponential-scale.description: Whether a scale move changes by a steady ratio. A zoom then looks even. From, to, or across 0, it moves at an even pace. It applies only to `scale`, `scale.x`, `scale.y`, `scale.z`, and `crop.scale`.

oscillate.description: A wave added to the value from this keyframe to the next, or to the step's end. On a looping curve, the wave plays again each time around.

amplitude.description: How far the value swings either way, in the parameter's own unit.

frequency.description: How many full cycles each second.

phase.description: Where in its cycle the wave starts. A cycle is 360 degrees. The default is 0.

wave-shape.description: The wave's shape. With a seed, it must be `noise`. The default is sine.

seed.description: The noise seed. The same seed gives the same noise. The default is 0.

keyframes.description: The keyframes, one or more, in any order: they are read by their time, then by their id.

loop.description: How it loops after its last keyframe until the step ends. With `repeat`, it replays from `loop-keyframe` to the last. With `ping-pong`, it plays that back and forth. Without it, it plays once.

loop-keyframe.description: The id of the keyframe the loop starts at. If the keyframe has a `start`, the loop begins with its move. If it names no keyframe of the curve, the first is used.

curves.description: The step's animation, by object and parameter, such as card.opacity.

items.description: An event at a set time in a step. A clip plays an Action of the GLB `file` of a model or a 3D text. A text built from an `extrusion` has no Actions. A clip on it plays nothing and causes a warning.

id.description: The cue's id, unique in its step among its keyframes and cues.

time.description: When it happens, in seconds into the step.

object.description: The id of the object it acts on: for a clip, a model or a 3D text.

paragraph.description: The id of the paragraph that appears. The id is in the `<!-- id: … -->` that ends the paragraph's last line. A reader warns when no paragraph of the text has the id.

id.description: The cue's id, unique in its step among its keyframes and cues.

time.description: When it happens, in seconds into the step.

object.description: The id of the object it acts on: for a clip, a model or a 3D text.

id.description: The cue's id, unique in its step among its keyframes and cues.

time.description: When it happens, in seconds into the step.

object.description: The id of the object it acts on: for a clip, a model or a 3D text.

id.description: The cue's id, unique in its step among its keyframes and cues.

time.description: When it happens, in seconds into the step.

object.description: The id of the object it acts on: for a clip, a model or a 3D text.

id.description: The cue's id, unique in its step among its keyframes and cues.

time.description: When it happens, in seconds into the step.

object.description: The id of the object it acts on: for a clip, a model or a 3D text.

action.description: The name of the Action that a clip plays. An unnamed Action is Animation 1, Animation 2, and so on, in file order.

loop.description: With `repeat`, the Action plays again from its start each time it ends. Without it, the Action plays once.

clip-trim.description: The part of the Action that plays, as a start and an end in seconds into the Action.

stride.description: How far the model travels per cycle of its Action, in the GLB's meters. The Action's timing then follows the model's travel. It doesn't apply to a 3D text's clip.

blend-in.description: How long the clip takes to blend in fully over the model's current motion. Without it, the clip is fully blended in from its start.

clip-scale.description: How much longer a clip's Action plays than its file says. 2 is half speed, and 0.5 is double. Maya's Clip Scale works the same way. The default is 1. It isn't used by a model's clip with a `stride`.

cues.description: Events at set times in the step, in any order: they are read by their time, then by their id. Each shows a paragraph, starts an audio object, a video or a web video, or plays a clip or an Action.

color.description: The color: a color role or a hex color.

position.description: Where the color is along the gradient, from 0 to 1. Without it, the first stop is at 0, the last is at 1, and the stops between are spread evenly. A stop is never before the previous one.

table-frame.description: An object's position and size, in canvas units from the slide's top left. A table's frame has only x and y. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text.

x.description: How far across the left edge is.

y.description: How far down the top edge is.

tail.description: The tip of a speech bubble's tail.

x.description: How far across the frame, as a fraction of its width.

y.description: How far down the frame, as a fraction of its height.

anyOf.description: A text's drop shadow. Its keys work like those of Photoshop's Drop Shadow. Its lengths are in ems of the text's font size. First, what the text paints, its letters and its outline, grows solid by size × spread. Then it is blurred by a Gaussian whose standard deviation is size × (1 − spread) / √6. The size isn't a blur radius.

size.description: How far past what the text paints the shadow reaches. Photoshop's Size works the same way.

spread.description: The fraction of the size that is solid. The rest of the size is blurred. At 1, the shadow is solid all the way out. Photoshop's Spread works the same way.

offset.description: How far the shadow falls, as {x, y} across and down in the text's own axes. It turns and scales with the text and its groups.

color.description: Its color: a color role, or a hex color written #RGB or #RRGGBB. A role's alpha is ignored. The shadow's opacity is set by `opacity` alone.

text-frame.description: An object's position and size, in canvas units from the slide's top left. A table's frame has only x and y. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text.

x.description: How far across the left edge is.

y.description: How far down the top edge is.

anyOf.description: A text's 3D model, in one of two forms. With an `extrusion`, MarkdownPoint builds the words' letters into a model. With a `file`, the model is a GLB that a program built, and `built-from` is the fingerprint of what it was built from. One unit of the model is one em of the text's size. Its origin is on the first line's baseline, at the left of the text's column. The model moves, turns, and scales with the text's frame. Its depth scales by the square root of the text's x scale times its y scale. A step's clips play the Actions of a GLB `file` the same way they play a model's. An `extrusion` has no Actions.

extrusion.description: The depth and bevel MarkdownPoint builds the words' letters to, in ems. With an empty record, the letters are built to the defaults.

depth.description: How far the letters stand out from the slide, in ems.

bevel.description: How far the letters' edges are rounded, in ems. At 0, they are sharp.

anyOf.description: A text's 3D model, in one of two forms. With an `extrusion`, MarkdownPoint builds the words' letters into a model. With a `file`, the model is a GLB that a program built, and `built-from` is the fingerprint of what it was built from. One unit of the model is one em of the text's size. Its origin is on the first line's baseline, at the left of the text's column. The model moves, turns, and scales with the text's frame. Its depth scales by the square root of the text's x scale times its y scale. A step's clips play the Actions of a GLB `file` the same way they play a model's. An `extrusion` has no Actions.

file.description: The GLB a program built from the words, as a presentation's file path.

built-from.description: The fingerprint of what the GLB was built from, by the rule the reference gives. A reader that doesn't know the rule treats the model as out of sync.

tilt.description: How far a group tilts in depth, in degrees, about axes through its anchor point in the slide's plane.

x.description: It turns about the horizontal axis. With a positive x, its top turns away from the viewer. CSS's `rotateX()` turns the same way. A 3D object turns the other way under a positive `rotation.x`.

y.description: It turns about the vertical axis. With a positive y, its left side comes forward. It turns after the group's rotation and before its x.

time-trim.description: The part of a video or audio file, or of a clip's Action, that plays.

start.description: Where it starts, in seconds into the file or the Action. The default is 0.

end.description: Where it ends, in seconds into the file or the Action. It must come after start. Without it, the file or the Action plays to its end.

transition.description: A slide transition. The defaults are interpolation ease-in-out, match object, direction left, color black, and delay 0.

start.description: When it starts. The default is a click. With `automatically`, it starts after the slide's last step.

delay.description: How long a transition that starts by itself waits after the slide's last step ends.

duration.description: How long it takes. It's left out when the effect is `none`.

match.description: What `carry-over` matches between two texts: whole objects, words, or characters.

utc-time.description: a UTC timestamp to the millisecond, such as "2026-10-17T19:30:00.000Z"

wipe.description: A reveal behind a moving straight edge.

progress.description: How much of the object shows. At 0, none of it shows. At 1, all of it shows.

angle.description: Which way the edge travels, in degrees clockwise from up. The angle turns with the object.

feather.description: How wide the soft edge is. Across it, the object fades from shown to hidden.
